headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Replit Agent can write and exfiltrate code/secrets, while awesome-python is a non-runnable docs-only collection with no protective runtime boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented between awesome-python and Replit Agent. The former is a non-runnable docs-only collection, while the latter operates inside a Replit workspace; there is no shared channel, clipboard, or MCP path shown in either profile.
conditions: IF a manual copy-paste bridge is introduced between the docs and the Replit workspace, injection risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the docs collection and Replit workspace separate.
Avoid copying untrusted text from the collection into agent prompts.
Use a human review step before pasting any generated instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-python touches no data classes and has no runtime, so it cannot leak by itself. Replit Agent can read/write Repl workspace files and handle secrets, but the pair lacks a documented shared filesystem or automatic data flow, so leakage requires an unusual manual bridge.
conditions: IF secrets or source code from the Replit workspace are manually copied into the docs workflow, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared notes or pasted prompts.
Store sensitive files outside any manually shared workspace.
Review copied content before sending it to either agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface to conflict over: awesome-python is not runnable and has no filesystem permissions, while Replit Agent writes only within a Repl workspace. Without a shared mutable resource, concurrent write conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable repository or workspace, write conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Keep the docs-only agent out of mutable project directories.
Use separate repositories for documentation and code generation.
If sharing a repo, add explicit locking or review gates.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-python does not generate operational actions, so Replit Agent is unlikely to treat its output as authoritative by default. Any cascade would require a manual workflow where docs content is copied into the coding agent, making the blast radius limited and non-default.
conditions: IF documentation snippets from awesome-python are pasted into Replit Agent as instructions, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Label pasted snippets as untrusted references.
Require verification before acting on copied guidance.
Keep implementation tasks separate from reference browsing.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance breach is evident from awesome-python alone because it is docs-only and touches no data classes. Replit Agent does handle secrets and deployment configuration, so compliance concerns arise only if regulated data is introduced into the Replit workspace; the other agent is not a direct compliance sink.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into the Replit workspace, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in the Replit workspace.
Use synthetic or redacted examples for development.
Confirm retention and residency settings before uploading sensitive material.
